This paper proves a scalar curvature constant and non-increasing Ricci curvature condition underpinnings theorem in two-dimensional geometry without voids. The proof relies on the established entropy framework developed by Li-Yau and Hamel, along with a novel estimate of the Ricci curvature gradient.

This study presents a transformative approach to image classification that integrates the flexibility of dynamic depth adjustments with the efficiency of shared computations. Our configurable architecture, CMAP-Net, combines a baseline network with an additional module that varies its structure based on specific instances, enhancing overall performance. We evaluated CMAP-Net's benefits by applying it to optimized versions of SqueezeNet and MobileNetV2, along with another optimized approach, ResPebbleNet, which skips zero-padding and activation functions in their repeated layers. The results show that CMAP-Net's improvements lead to state-of-the-art accuracy rates for Modified SqueezeNet and MobileNetV2 variants, without incurring extra computational costs, and also demonstrate benefits when applied to ResPebbleNet. Furthermore, we analyzed the distribution of structural learning's adjustments and found that they tend to occur in the network's initial layers, aligning with existing research findings, and confirmed that proposed performance gains are not due to changes in feature space dimensions.

Educational frameworks within Federated Learning enable clients to train the global model along with contributing local data. Typically, servers select models for distribution while clients only passively receive them. In a "Random Stroll," a client's model can be customized based on their data characteristics. This paper introduces a novel approach, a "Purposeful Stroll for Education," where the server tailors model distribution to optimize learning outcomes. A uniform distribution strategy is employed to minimize communication costs. Local data heterogeneity is addressed using clustering techniques. A client may opt-out of global model updates at any time. Through simulations, our method outperforms traditional approaches in terms of accuracy and speedup, demonstrating its effectiveness.

This study presents a consistency regularization method using average
values for semi-supervised medical image segmentation that is straightforward
yet requires verification for its novel status. Despite existing theory supporting
the use of average value-based methods for consistency regularization, which are
believed to be equivalent, practical implementations often face challenges due
to numerical instability. A modified approach is therefore suggested, utilizing
a simple adjustment that has proven effective in practice. Experimental results
obtained through various data splits of the ORigaMCl dataset demonstrate the
efficacy of the proposed modification, surpassing both randomly sampled baselines
and alternative consistency regularization techniques using variance. Furthermore,
the integration of additional labelled samples is found to enhance performance.

We resolve the apparent paradox of our observation: a single photon's interference pattern results from genuine nonlocal entanglement within the photon itself. In a setup where a single photon interferes with itself, we found that the nonlocal part of the entanglement between the photon's two position states contributes significantly to guiding the photon. Consequently, the entanglement between the two possible positions plays a crucial role in determining the interference pattern observed.

This research provides an comprehensive overview of integrating blockchain technology into federated educational systems tailored for internet-of-vehicles environments. As autonomous vehicle technologies advance, maintaining up-to-date and efficient knowledge within these systems is increasingly important, leading to the exploration of customized and federated educational approaches as well as the potential role of blockchain technology in these frameworks. Our comprehensive document outlines various customized and federated educational methods, analyzes the contribution of blockchain technology to these systems, identifies technical challenges, and discusses possible solutions and future directions.

Deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) have excelled in various natural language processing tasks but suffer from large sizes. In contrast, Tuber Neural Networks (TNN) are efficient and suitable for hardware implementation but lack capacity to handle complex tasks. This paper proposes a novel hybrid Architecture LSTM-Tensor, combining the best of both networks to overcome their individual limitations. Research shows that this new design performs as well or even better than large LSTMs and small TNNs. Furthermore, we developed an efficient hardware design for the new architecture on a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform with hardware sharing techniques, achieving real-time video identification with high accuracy while significantly improving speed and energy efficiency compared to the original model.

This study systematically examines higher power iterations of the composition of two polynomials, beginning with iterative methods suitable for use with wide variations in initial values. It delves into whether certain mathematical properties persist through these iterates and explores connecting various existing mathematical theories. A comprehensive collection of examples is provided to illustrate the concepts discussed, along with the presentation of new findings.

Our study addresses solutions to the Schrödinger equation outside convex domains that are influenced by a nonlinear source term. We establish that explosive solutions occur explosive solutions occur when initial values are sufficiently close to the domain. Moreover, we identify the critical threshold that separates solutions with and without explosion, and determine the exact time of explosion for those that occur. These findings are new and insightful.

Following the concept of local rational parameterization introduced by Lombardi and Quela, this local local parametric parameterization has been rebranded, with the new method yielding a evidence of Borger's local embedding theorem in positive characteristic settings, along with a enhancement over the original proof, along with a improvement over the original demonstration.

Bayes factors are highly sensitive to sample size, exhibiting extreme values that can be both supportive and oversupportive of hypotheses. This characteristic poses a significant obstacle to formulating a decision rule based solely on Bayes factors. However, integrating additional considerations, such as effect sizes and model criticism, enables the development of a comprehensive workflow that leverages Bayes factors effectively. We present an original decision-analytic approach that accommodates various practical scenarios and can be applied to existing data for calculating the probability of obtaining beneficial new data in future studies. This information facilitates the planning of more informative experiments, potentially in an amplified form, to elicit decisive results from Bayes factors. We illustrate this methodology using simulated data from studies examining the absence of an effect, its presence, and the non-existence of differences, both within and across groups.

Recent years have seen a surge in research utilizing discourse indicators or discourse markers in various tasks such as summarization, classification, and question answering. However, the significance of these elements in text understanding and analysis tasks has been lacking in in-depth investigation. To address this void, we conducted an extensive study on the role of discourse indicators, examining 14 commonly used indicators through multiple tasks including classification, regression, and text labeling, and leveraging an already existing model for initial text understanding tasks. Findings from our research reveal that the effectiveness of discourse indicators varies significantly across different tasks and even within the same task but with differing objectives or training data sets. To overcome these challenges, we developed a new training method that incorporates multi-task learning and a unique training data collection process, resulting in a new model that achieves superior performance over existing approaches through multiple evaluation metrics such as pearson, spearman, F1, and accuracy scores across multiple tasks. Our study not only contribute technically but also provide valuable insights linguistically on the function of discourse indicators in text understanding.

Recently introduced is the Jordanian twist operator, initially developed by Isham and Jammer in 1973 and more extensively examined by Isham in 2018. This operator's primary characteristic lies in its capacity to partition the Einstein universe solution space of the Jordan-Dicke-Scott equation into distinct sections through its application repeatedly. A generalization of this operator is presented in this study enabling users to observe its behavior graphically as a function of a specific parameter. Furthermore, the paper identifies equivalent expressions of the modified twist operator based on the original formulation by Isham and a variant explored by Braat and Dickson in 1950.

This study aims to algebraically solve the containment problem for a specialized form of regular expressions, referred to as XREs. By integrating the Brzozowski derivative concept with the forward pre-image operation, we develop an algorithm that can efficiently resolve this containment problem. Our method leverages the Dreyer-Narod right context theorem to convert (I + A*)* pre-image problems into (I + A*)* containment pre-image problems, and utilizes the Brzozowski derivative to resolve these simplified problems. We base our work on the Nguyen-Ferrere-Senulita et al. regular expression matching approach, which our team extends to address XREs, incorporating patterns for the +, *, ?, *,*,+,*, and () operators, as well as the *+ and *m,*n operators. Our proposed solution provides an algorithmic solution to the (I + A*)* containment pre-image problem, which can be applied to security protocols to enhance their safety by resolving state-based regulations within automata systems.

Building upon previous work (arXiv:1601.00577, arXiv:1602.00954), we derive a generalized form of a specific four-point function in CFT$_2$ where a product of two primary fields is involved in an annular region, utilizing the conformal block decomposition applicable to this configuration. This four-point function within a ring is key to developing a non-linear evolution equation, analogous to the BK equation in high energy physics, within the $\phi^4$ quantum field theory model. By utilizing the correspondence between AdS$_{2}$ and CFT$_{2}$, we further extend this non-linear equation to the $\phi^4$ model in AdS$_{2}$. Notably, we find that the BK equation in this context is equivalent to a linear Schrödinger equation in a higher-dimensional space, specifically a hypercylinder in AdS$_{3}$, thus establishing a new multi-point bulk interaction-CFT multi-point function correspondence, even for non-protected operators, within the large-N limit of the theory.

To expand the field of view lobster-eye lenses have been arranged in a multiplexed configuration, consisting of nine rows with ten lenses in each row and a central row with 17 lenses. A test setup with nine source locations and ten detector locations was created to evaluate the performance of this arrangement. Results showed that specific source-detection pairs have reduced signal quality due to occlusion and aliasing issues but overall the configuration effectively reduces data requirements while maintaining a wide field of view. A proposed setup with 81 lobster-eye lenses could cover a field of view of 90 degrees and a total active area of 2 square meters, making it suitable for building a broad-field X-ray monitoring detector large in area and number of resolvable sources.

To predict the dark matter halo mass spectrum across the universe, deep learning has successfully leveraged the concept of halo overdensity as an observation variable. This paper aims to explore the efficacy of substituting halo overdensity with halo velocity dispersion as the observation variable for generating the dark matter halo mass distribution. Our research found that training a model to predict halo velocity dispersion was considerably more challenging than halo overdensity. Moreover, we observed that halo velocity dispersion fails to reconstruct the dark matter halo mass spectrum effectively on smaller scales. To investigate this limitation, we analyzed the correlation between velocity dispersion and overdensity in our simulated universe. Our findings revealed that overdensity is generally more effective than velocity dispersion in capturing information about large-scale structures. Based on these insights, we produced modified models to enhance the correlation between velocity and overdensity on smaller scales. In this adjusted environment, we discovered that dark matter halos velocity dispersion can effectively predict halo mass on larger scales, demonstrating the potential of utilizing hydrodynamics-derived information to improve cosmological parameter estimation. However, we observed that models predicting velocity-related data were still less effective than those processing density-related information. To further analyze this outcome, we examined the relationship between initial density and velocity perturbations. Our analysis revealed that initial velocity perturbations are intrinsically correlated with density perturbuations, enabling hydro information to infer cosmological parameters but not local mass information. This research highlights the importance of large-scale structure on cosmological parameter estimation and the necessity of incorporating mass resolution in simulations for

Atomic interferometry offers exceptional sensitivity to magnetic fields, enabling precise measurements, but is limited by the insensitivity to constant magnetic field strengths. To overcome this restriction and allow for precise measurements of varying magnetic fields locally, our research proposes combining atomic interferometry with the local Meissner effect produced by a moving superconductor. This method is capable of detecting minute magnetic field variations close to the Meissner source through atomic interferometry, taking advantage of the sharp boundary created by the superconductor's expulsion of magnetic fields. This system's sensitivity is limited by the sensitivity of atomic interferometry and can be as high as $10^{-4}$ nT$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}^{-1}}$ with an atom interferometer with an oscillation time of a few seconds, which is sensitive to magnetic field variations at a microscopic scale, which is important for several quantum optics experiments. This combination of the SQUID amplifier and atomic interferometry may lead to the development of a powerful magnetometer that is capable of detecting local magnetic field changes, which can be utilized to observe the spontaneous symmetry breaking and the emergence of spin-orbit coupling in cold atom systems.

This study formulates an initiative framework for developing theories of non-equilibrium states in superconducting systems, enabling the prediction of Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) state spectra. This methodology integrates a focus on magnetic adatoms resting on superconducting substrates to develop specific predictions for adatom configurations and arrangements to anticipate spectral characteristics of these particular configurations and arrangements. This framework draws upon initial principles of statistical physics to establish an approach that allows for the determination of local density of states on superconducting films by simulating various external field distributions acting upon the adatoms and superconducting films. This approach proves particularly effective in anticipating the spectral characteristics of magnetic adatoms and their clusters residing on superconducting films and leads to the development of an initiative strategy for developing a complete theory of nonequilibrium states in superconducting systems.

This study addresses the need for accurate and efficient skin cancer diagnosis by leveraging a deep learning approach that incorporates an outlier detection method called DISKODDODD. Outlier detection, a technique under concept drift, has not been extensively applied to medical diagnosis until now. To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed method, we utilized the largest available skin cancer dataset, which contains 130,000 images of five different skin lesions, to train a deep neural network. The model's performance was measured using five different evaluation metrics, and it was also compared to other existing methods. Furthermore, the entire dataset was randomly divided into ten subsets to simulate an abnormal distribution in a portion of the data, which was then identified and excluded by the deep learning model combined with Outlier Detection to enhance overall performance. The results obtained from this experiment, along with outcomes from one additional experiment, demonstrated the efficacy of the proposed method. Additionally, the entire process was found to be highly efficient, making it feasible for clinical use.

Due to its enhanced sensitivity and broad scope, low-energy muon spectroscopy is being considered as a powerful method for searching for new physics beyond the standard model. To identify potential new physics, it is crucial to have a precise understanding of muon-spin-dependent interactions with matter, which consist of both ordinary interactions with charged particles deep inelastic scattering and a lower probability of weak interactions involving vector bosons. While QED models accurately predict the distribution of virtuality among vector bosons available for weak interactions, more precise estimates are necessary to effectively search for new physics. To achieve this, an efficient algorithm has been developed based on the matrix element of deep inelastic scattering, allowing for the calculation of vector boson distributions in muons in both polarized and unpolarized states, which can be applied to large samples of target particles for searching new physics.

This paper presents the fundamental findings of mathematicians Tarski, Godel, Carnap, and Carnap along with a new theorem by Rosser that follows from their work. While Godel's first incompleteness theorem demonstrates the existence of unprovable statements within formal arithmetic, it relies on the fixed-point lemma, which has various forms applicable to increasingly complex logical systems. Although Godel's proof of the second incompleteness theorem and meta-mathematical research conducted by Rosser, Godel, Tarski, and Carnap mainly apply to first-order arithmetic, a comparable inquiry can be conducted within a more comprehensive theory that includes a recursive function symbol, resulting in an enhanced version of the classical findings.

This study examines the invariant behavior of fractional-order dynamical systems when treated as a subsystem within a higher-dimensional framework, specifically focusing on the role of the third state variable. We demonstrate that both linear and nonlinear quadratic systems of fractional-order do not have invariant lines or parabolas in the (x,y)-plane due to the leakage of the third state variable when the order of that variable's derivative is sufficiently low. We provide new insights into the dynamics of fractional-order systems by developing a set of conditions that ensure invariant curves, analogous to what has been commonly used in second-order integer systems. We apply these conditions to a variety of third-order integer systems of both linear and nonlinear types, showing their relevance to the behavior of fractional-order versions of these systems.

This study investigates an inverse problem in which the source characteristics of a loudspeaker are unknown. Despite the source's time-varying and unknown nature, the goal is to use a single sensor's data to estimate the room's eigenmodes, predict the room's acoustic response at a specific point, and even modify this response. Initially, the loudspeaker's impulse response is captured, and the sensor's response to this impulse is obtained. By analyzing this response, the room's modal characteristics are identified using a subspace method, leading to a model of the room's acoustic environment. This model is then refined through a least-squares optimization process, allowing for more accurate prediction of the room's response and potential control of it at a specific frequency. Ultimately, the system demonstrates the feasibility of structural acoustic control in a room, achieving a reduction in error by three orders of magnitude. Although unverified with listener tests, the results suggest the possibility of controlled acoustic environments, paving the way for potential applications such as localized silence and enhanced speech recognition in previously untreated spaces.

Within the simplest variant of the scoto-seesaw model, our research delves into both vacuum stability and fermion mass generation mechanisms. Specifically, we examine the origin of the neutrino mass through the secoto-seesaw effect as well as the generation of the mass for the charged Higgs particle via mixing. Furthermore, we investigate the potential for neutral current neutrino oscillation or like-with-like particle production of the heavy neutral fermions, referred to as the "wimps," and assess its feasibility. In addition, we explore the mechanism by which the charged Higgs particle may have contributed to the peak observed in the dwarf galaxy spectrum of neutral current neutrino oscillations. Lastly, we confirm that within the parameters of the least unstable variant of the model, specifically one that satisfies all current experimental constraints and theoretical requirements, including the "wino-like" nature of the dark matter particle, a small but direct coupling of the charged Higgs to the electron is made possible, potentially explaining the dip observed in an inversion of the neutrino mass sequence known as the "secoto-seesaw" model.
